opening.text: Think of a small child walking through a dark room. She cannot see the floor. But she is holding her father’s hand. So she walks without fear.
That is what trust looks like. She does not know the way. She knows the one who does. Today I want to talk about trusting God.

mainMessage.text: Trust in God means we rely on Him even when we cannot see the path. He is near. He knows what we do not. His will and timing are good. Trust is tested in hard times, and it grows in the waiting. And when we trust Him, we are willing to act.

blocks.text: Trust begins in the heart.
Solomon taught that we should trust in the Lord with all our heart, and not lean on our own understanding. Isaiah wrote that God is our salvation, and so we need not be afraid.
Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths.
Behold, God is my salvation; I will trust, and not be afraid; for the Lord Jehovah is my strength and my song; he also has become my salvation.
Elder Richard G. Scott of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “To Be Healed” from the April 1994 general conference.

Faith in Christ means we trust Him; we trust His teachings. That leads to hope, and hope brings charity, the pure love of Christ—that peaceful feeling that comes when we sense His concern, His love, and His capacity to cure us or to ease our burdens with His healing power.
Trust is more than a thought. It is a leaning of the heart.
He is near.
The child in the dark is not alone. Neither are we. The psalmist called God a very present help in trouble. And the Lord told Isaiah’s people not to fear, for He is with them.
God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble. Therefore will not we fear, though the earth be removed, and though the mountains be carried into the midst of the sea;
Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Jesus Christ—the Master Healer” from the October 2005 general conference.

I know that feeling! I know the fears and tears of such moments. But I also know that our prayers are never ignored. Our faith is never unappreciated. I know that an all-wise Heavenly Father’s perspective is much broader than is ours. While we know of our mortal problems and pain, He knows of our immortal progress and potential. If we pray to know His will and submit ourselves to it with patience and courage, heavenly healing can take place in His own way and time.
He does not leave us alone in the dark.
His will and His timing are good.

We often want answers now, in the way we picture them. God sees more. Alma taught his son to counsel with the Lord in all things. Moroni taught that faith in God gives us a hope that holds us steady like an anchor.

Counsel with the Lord in all thy doings, and he will direct thee for good; yea, when thou liest down at night lie down unto the Lord, that he may watch over you in your sleep; and when thou risest in the morning let thy heart be full of thanks unto God; and if ye do these things, ye shall be lifted up at the last day.

Wherefore, whoso believeth in God might with surety hope for a better world, yea, even a place at the right hand of God, which hope cometh of faith, maketh an anchor to the souls of men, which would make them sure and steadfast, always abounding in good works, being led to glorify God.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles wrote this in his article “The Atonement and Faith” in the April 2010 Ensign. It is a magazine article, not a conference talk.

No matter how strong our faith is, it cannot produce a result contrary to the will of Him in whom we have faith. Remember that when your prayers do not seem to be answered in the way or at the time you desire. The exercise of faith in the Lord Jesus Christ is always subject to the order of heaven, to the goodness and will and wisdom and timing of the Lord. When we have that kind of faith and trust in the Lord, we have true security and serenity in our lives.
Trust gives us peace, even before we have every answer.
Trust is tested in hard times.

Three young men stood before a king and a furnace. They said God could save them. And then they said something braver: even if He did not, they would still be faithful. Alma told his son that those who trust God will be supported in their trials.

Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, answered and said to the king, O Nebuchadnezzar, we are not careful to answer thee in this matter. If it be so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace, and he will deliver us out of thine hand, O king. But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up.

And now, O my son Helaman, behold, thou art in thy youth, and therefore, I beseech of thee that thou wilt hear my words and learn of me; for I do know that whosoever shall put their trust in God shall be supported in their trials, and their troubles, and their afflictions, and shall be lifted up at the last day.
Elder Richard G. Scott of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Trust in the Lord” from the October 1995 general conference.

Testing . . . is needed even when you are living a worthy, righteous life and are obedient to \[God’s\] commandments. Just when all seems to be going right, challenges often come in multiple doses applied simultaneously.
Hard times do not mean God has left. They are often where trust grows.
Trust grows in the waiting.

Waiting is hard. Moses told frightened Israel to stand still and see the salvation of the Lord. King Limhi told his people that if they turned to the Lord and put their trust in Him, He would deliver them.

And Moses said unto the people, Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the Lord, which he will shew to you to day: for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to day, ye shall see them again no more for ever. The Lord shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace.

But if ye will turn to the Lord with full purpose of heart, and put your trust in him, and serve him with all diligence of mind, if ye do this, he will, according to his own will and pleasure, deliver you out of bondage.
Elder Neal A. Maxwell of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Willing to Submit” from the April 1985 general conference.
Just as the capacity to defer gratification is a sign of real maturity, likewise the willingness to wait for deferred explanation is a sign of real faith and of trust spread over time.
Some answers come late. Trust is what carries us until they do.
Trust leads us to act.

Trust is not only waiting. It moves our feet. Nephi said he would go and do what the Lord commanded, because the Lord prepares a way. Mormon’s record shows the Lord blesses and prospers those who put their trust in Him.

And it came to pass that I, Nephi, said unto my father: I will go and do the things which the Lord hath commanded, for I know that the Lord giveth no commandments unto the children of men, save he shall prepare a way for them that they may accomplish the thing which he commandeth them.

And thus we can behold how false, and also the unsteadiness of the hearts of the children of men; yea, we can see that the Lord in his great infinite goodness doth bless and prosper those who put their trust in him.
President Henry B. Eyring of the First Presidency said this in his talk “Act in All Diligence” from the April 2010 general conference.

This is the Lord’s Church. He called us and trusted us even in the weaknesses He knew we had. He knew the trials we would face. By faithful service and through His Atonement, we can come to want what He wants and be what we must be to bless those we serve for Him. As we serve Him long enough and with diligence, we will be changed. We can become ever more like Him.
God trusts us. We can trust Him back.

story.title: Peter walks on the water

blocks.text: The disciples saw Jesus Christ walking on the sea in a storm. Peter asked to come to Him.

And Peter answered him and said, Lord, if it be thou, bid me come unto thee on the water. And he said, Come. And when Peter was come down out of the ship, he walked on the water, to go to Jesus. But when he saw the wind boisterous, he was afraid; and beginning to sink, he cried, saying, Lord, save me. And immediately Jesus stretched forth his hand, and caught him, and said unto him, O thou of little faith, wherefore didst thou doubt?
Peter walked while he looked at Jesus. He sank when he looked at the wind. But notice this. When he cried out, the Savior caught him at once. Trust is not never doubting. It is turning back to Him.

story.title: The widow gives her last meal

blocks.text: A famine was in the land. A widow in Zarephath had only a handful of flour and a little oil. The prophet Elijah asked her to feed him first.

And she said, As the Lord thy God liveth, I have not a cake, but an handful of meal in a barrel, and a little oil in a cruse: and, behold, I am gathering two sticks, that I may go in and dress it for me and my son, that we may eat it, and die. And Elijah said unto her, Fear not; go and do as thou hast said: but make me thereof a little cake first, and bring it unto me, and after make for thee and for thy son. For thus saith the Lord God of Israel, The barrel of meal shall not waste, neither shall the cruse of oil fail, until the day that the Lord sendeth rain upon the earth. And she went and did according to the saying of Elijah: and she, and he, and her house, did eat many days. And the barrel of meal wasted not, neither did the cruse of oil fail, according to the word of the Lord, which he spake by Elijah.
She did not see the whole trail. She only saw her last meal. She trusted, and she took the step. And the flour and oil did not run out.

story.title: Alma’s people and their burdens

blocks.text: Alma and his people were in bondage. They prayed in their hearts. And the Lord answered.

And it came to pass that the voice of the Lord came to them in their afflictions, saying: Lift up your heads and be of good comfort, for I know of the covenant which ye have made unto me; and I will covenant with my people and deliver them out of bondage. And I will also ease the burdens which are put upon your shoulders, that even you cannot feel them upon your backs, even while you are in bondage; and this will I do that ye may stand as witnesses for me hereafter, and that ye may know of a surety that I, the Lord God, do visit my people in their afflictions. And now it came to pass that the burdens which were laid upon Alma and his brethren were made light; yea, the Lord did strengthen them that they could bear up their burdens with ease, and they did submit cheerfully and with patience to all the will of the Lord.
The bondage did not end that day. But the burdens grew light. God did not remove the weight at once. He gave them strength to carry it. That is also a kind of rescue.

Trusting Christ means trusting what He teaches, even when we cannot see.
He is in the cockpit with us.
We are not flying alone. The psalmist called God a very present help. The Lord told His people, fear not, I am with thee.
God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble. Therefore will not we fear, though the earth be removed, and though the mountains be carried into the midst of the sea;
Fear thou not; for I am with thee: be not dismayed; for I am thy God: I will strengthen thee; yea, I will help thee; yea, I will uphold thee with the right hand of my righteousness.
Elder Russell M. Nelson of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Jesus Christ—the Master Healer” from the October 2005 general conference.

I know that feeling! I know the fears and tears of such moments. But I also know that our prayers are never ignored. Our faith is never unappreciated. I know that an all-wise Heavenly Father’s perspective is much broader than is ours. While we know of our mortal problems and pain, He knows of our immortal progress and potential. If we pray to know His will and submit ourselves to it with patience and courage, heavenly healing can take place in His own way and time.
His view is wider than ours. That is why we can rely on it.
Follow the instruments, not the fog.
In the fog, feelings say, “Do it my way.” God says, counsel with Me. Alma taught his son to counsel with the Lord in all things. Moroni taught that faith gives us a hope like an anchor.

Counsel with the Lord in all thy doings, and he will direct thee for good; yea, when thou liest down at night lie down unto the Lord, that he may watch over you in your sleep; and when thou risest in the morning let thy heart be full of thanks unto God; and if ye do these things, ye shall be lifted up at the last day.

Wherefore, whoso believeth in God might with surety hope for a better world, yea, even a place at the right hand of God, which hope cometh of faith, maketh an anchor to the souls of men, which would make them sure and steadfast, always abounding in good works, being led to glorify God.
Elder Dallin H. Oaks of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles wrote this in his article “The Atonement and Faith” in the April 2010 Ensign. It is a magazine article, not a conference talk.

No matter how strong our faith is, it cannot produce a result contrary to the will of Him in whom we have faith. Remember that when your prayers do not seem to be answered in the way or at the time you desire. The exercise of faith in the Lord Jesus Christ is always subject to the order of heaven, to the goodness and will and wisdom and timing of the Lord. When we have that kind of faith and trust in the Lord, we have true security and serenity in our lives.
Trust in His will brings calm.
Turbulence comes.

Even the best pilots meet turbulence. It does not mean the plane is failing. Three young men faced a furnace and said that even if God did not save them, they would not bow. Alma taught that those who trust God are supported in trials.

Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-nego, answered and said to the king, O Nebuchadnezzar, we are not careful to answer thee in this matter. If it be so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace, and he will deliver us out of thine hand, O king. But if not, be it known unto thee, O king, that we will not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up.

And now, O my son Helaman, behold, thou art in thy youth, and therefore, I beseech of thee that thou wilt hear my words and learn of me; for I do know that whosoever shall put their trust in God shall be supported in their trials, and their troubles, and their afflictions, and shall be lifted up at the last day.
Elder Richard G. Scott of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Trust in the Lord” from the October 1995 general conference.

Testing . . . is needed even when you are living a worthy, righteous life and are obedient to \[God’s\] commandments. Just when all seems to be going right, challenges often come in multiple doses applied simultaneously.
Turbulence is part of the flight. It is not the end of it.
Hold steady.

In the cloud, the answer is to hold steady. Moses told Israel to stand still and see the Lord’s salvation. Limhi told his people that if they turned to the Lord and trusted Him, He would deliver them.

And Moses said unto the people, Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the Lord, which he will shew to you to day: for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to day, ye shall see them again no more for ever. The Lord shall fight for you, and ye shall hold your peace.

But if ye will turn to the Lord with full purpose of heart, and put your trust in him, and serve him with all diligence of mind, if ye do this, he will, according to his own will and pleasure, deliver you out of bondage.
Elder Neal A. Maxwell of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles said this in his talk “Willing to Submit” from the April 1985 general conference.
Just as the capacity to defer gratification is a sign of real maturity, likewise the willingness to wait for deferred explanation is a sign of real faith and of trust spread over time.
We may not see the runway yet. It is still there.
Trust shows in how we fly.

A pilot who trusts her instruments acts on them. Nephi said he would go and do what the Lord commanded, for the Lord prepares a way. Mormon saw that those who trust in the Lord are blessed and prospered.

And it came to pass that I, Nephi, said unto my father: I will go and do the things which the Lord hath commanded, for I know that the Lord giveth no commandments unto the children of men, save he shall prepare a way for them that they may accomplish the thing which he commandeth them.

And thus we can behold how false, and also the unsteadiness of the hearts of the children of men; yea, we can see that the Lord in his great infinite goodness doth bless and prosper those who put their trust in him.
President Henry B. Eyring of the First Presidency said this in his talk “Act in All Diligence” from the April 2010 general conference.

This is the Lord’s Church. He called us and trusted us even in the weaknesses He knew we had. He knew the trials we would face. By faithful service and through His Atonement, we can come to want what He wants and be what we must be to bless those we serve for Him. As we serve Him long enough and with diligence, we will be changed. We can become ever more like Him.
He trusts us. We can act on that.

story.title: The Savior calms the storm

blocks.text: The disciples were crossing a lake at night. A great storm came. Jesus Christ was asleep in the boat.

And there arose a great storm of wind, and the waves beat into the ship, so that it was now full. And he was in the hinder part of the ship, asleep on a pillow: and they awake him, and say unto him, Master, carest thou not that we perish? And he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm. And he said unto them, Why are ye so fearful? how is it that ye have no faith?
The disciples feared the storm. The Savior was not afraid. He was in the boat with them the whole time. When we cannot see calm, we can remember who is in the boat.

story.title: Nephi follows the Liahona

blocks.text: Nephi’s bow had broken, and his family was hungry. He did not know where to find food. The Liahona showed him where to go.

And it came to pass that I, Nephi, did go forth up into the top of the mountain, according to the directions which were given upon the ball. And it came to pass that I did slay wild beasts, insomuch that I did obtain food for our families. And it came to pass that I did return to our tents, bearing the beasts which I had slain; and now when they beheld that I had obtained food, how great was their joy! And it came to pass that they did humble themselves before the Lord, and did give thanks unto him.
Nephi followed directions he did not fully understand. He went up the mountain because he trusted the One who gave them. And a hungry family was fed. Trust turned into food on the table.
